item.title: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
item.description:
What Is Vitamin B3 (Niacin)?

Vitamin B3, also known as niacin, nicotinic acid, or vitamin PP (pellagra-preventing), exists as multiple chemical entities with different biochemical functions and biohacking implications. Understanding these distinctions is critical for optimizing outcomes:

Nicotinic Acid (Niacin): The original form recognized to prevent pellagra (severe deficiency disease); provides the flush response and most potent therapeutic effects on lipid profiles and NAD+ elevation.

Nicotinamide (Niacinamide): The non-flushing form; functions as a direct NAD+ precursor but lacks the lipid-modifying and flushing effects of nicotinic acid—important distinction for protocol selection.

item.title: Berberine
item.description:
What Is Berberine?

Berberine is a naturally occurring alkaloid found in several plants including goldenseal, barberry, and Oregon grape. This bright yellow compound has been used in traditional Chinese and Ayurvedic medicine for centuries, primarily for gastrointestinal and infectious conditions.

In the last 15 years, berberine has become prominent in Western functional medicine due to its remarkable effects on blood sugar, lipid metabolism, and weight management—often rivaling pharmaceutical interventions like metformin while remaining entirely natural and widely available.

item.title: Supplements for Statin Users: Protecting Your Health While Managing Cholesterol
item.description:
Medical Disclaimer

This guide is for educational purposes and does not constitute medical advice. Statins are critical cardiovascular medications for many people. Always consult your cardiologist or prescribing physician before starting any supplement, as some can interact with cholesterol medications or affect blood lipid levels. Never discontinue or reduce statin therapy without professional medical guidance. Regular monitoring and professional oversight are essential.

Understanding Statin Therapy and Nutritional Support

Statins (like atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, pravastatin) are among the most widely prescribed medications for managing cholesterol and reducing cardiovascular disease risk. While effective at lowering cholesterol and potentially saving lives, statins have notable side effects and create specific nutritional deficiencies that can be addressed through targeted supplementation.
